Second row reads 'Developer load into this Rancher' with a server glyph and the note 'Studio's "This Rancher" publish: it builds in the pod and points this Rancher at the result. Reversible with "Remove local install".' - the design's 'still iteration' point is made by the row's reason, which says a developer load reaches only this Rancher and is ungated by design.
First row reads 'Your dev preview', carries an 'always' chip and a lock glyph, and is drawn with settings__dest--muted (greyed). Note: 'Hot reload while you work. Nobody else can load it.'

There is no OCI row. The row carrying the 'The gate' chip and the green settings__dest--gate highlight is 'Push to a repository' (GitHub), and its own note says so: 'Studio pushes to GitHub; it cannot push an OCI artifact, so the design's OCI row is this one.'
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: no OCI destination exists in this product, so the highlighted gate row is a GitHub source push standing in for it. The highlight and the tag are drawn correctly on the row that is actually the gate; nothing to fix until an OCI push exists.

verdicts.evidence: Clicked 'Notified' on the developer-load code-review control: it moved to Notified. Reloaded /barn/settings and it was still Notified. Clicked 'Off' and it went back, and the ConfigMap barn-studio-settings ended at dev-load.code = off. The control now offers two segments rather than the design's three - 'Required' has been removed deliberately, because a developer load is ungated and nothing could obey it - but the effect the design asks for (choose the level, it sticks, no save step) happens.

The control is now two-way: only 'Off' and 'Notified' render, so 'Required' cannot be selected at all. Seeded ConfigMap barn-studio-settings with dev-load {code: required, outcome: required} by kubectl and loaded the page: it drew Notified/Notified and wrote notified/notified straight back into the ConfigMap, so a stored 'required' reconciles down on load. Setting 'Notified' does have a real effect - the publish dialog's 'Load into this Rancher' row then reads the chip 'Sign-offs advisory' and the note 'Settings ask to be notified of an outcome sign-off here... they never hold this destination up.'
verdicts.defect: The design's promise (set Required and a developer load demands an outcome sign-off) still cannot happen, and is now not even offerable: Required has been removed from this row because a developer load is ungated by design. The previous defect - a Required that was stored and then openly ignored by the publish dialog - is gone. What is left is a two-way control where the design draws three.

verdicts.evidence: Dev preview code-review control: 'Off' selected, all three segments disabled. Force-clicked 'Notified': still Off.
Dev preview outcome control: 'Off' selected, all three segments disabled. Force-clicked 'Required': still Off.

Clicked Restart on the nodehealth row (chosen over base to avoid disturbing other verifiers' pods). Before: pod barn-nodehealth-extension-58f64c4997-mlt29, startTime 19:53:37, row 'Dev server running - uptime 3h 11m'. Immediately after: pod barn-nodehealth-extension-58f64c4997-xss66, startTime 23:05:34, row 'Pod running, not serving yet - uptime 0m'. Half a minute later the row read 'Dev server running - uptime 0m'. So the button really deletes the pod and the Deployment replaces it, and the uptime resets.

Three rows, one per extension pod in namespace barn: base 'Dev server running - uptime 1d 16h', demo 'Dev server running - uptime 17h 44m', nodehealth 'Dev server running - uptime 2h 29m', each with settings__dot--on (green). The uptimes track the pods' real container start times, and after the nodehealth restart the row moved through the amber 'Pod running, not serving yet' state before going green again.

The row and its machinery work, but the connected state cannot be reached here. Pasting a token makes the browser spend it against api.github.com first; a 401 comes back (verified directly: fetch('https://api.github.com/user') with a fake bearer returns 401 from this browser), so connectGithub throws TokenRejected, nothing is stored, and the field shows 'GitHub rejected that token, so it has not been stored.' To see the stored path I seeded Secret barn-settings with a gh_token key and the barn.rancher.io/gh-token=set annotation: the card then read 'A token is stored', chip 'Rejected by GitHub' (s-chip--warning), and 'GitHub rejected the token (Bad credentials). Reconnect with a replacement; the one stored now will fail the next import or push.' - GitHub's real 401, asked from a pod. The Active pill, the login, the scopes and the expiry all need a token GitHub accepts, and no such token exists in this environment. Secret restored to empty afterwards.

With a token stored (seeded into Secret barn-settings), the card showed 'A token is stored' + Disconnect. Clicked Disconnect: the card fell back to 'Not connected', the Disconnect button disappeared, and kubectl showed the Secret with no data keys and the barn.rancher.io/gh-token annotation removed. The second half of the design's check does not hold: the publish dialog's 'Push the source to GitHub' row is still offered and still tickable with no token (verified before and after) - what refuses is the next dialog, which shows 'There is no GitHub token yet, and pushing needs one' and disables its Publish button. The gated 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' row does track the token: its reason changed from 'No GitHub token is configured, so this Studio cannot push anywhere' to 'No repository is remembered for this extension yet' while the token was stored.

The card head states the two uses (import, push, and the pull request) but explicitly declines the isolation promise: 'Generated extensions are never handed this credential, but the pod they run in can read the Secret it lives in (barn-settings in namespace barn, and that pod is bound to cluster-admin), so treat it as a credential Studio shares with anything it runs.'
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's promise that a generated extension never gets this credential is not true here and the card says so rather than repeating it. Making it true means running extension pods under a ServiceAccount that is not cluster-admin, or keeping the token out of a namespace those pods can read.

verdicts.evidence: Clicked Connect: a password-type 'GitHub token' field appears and takes focus, with the hint 'Press Enter to store it' and a PAT note linking to https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo&description=Rancher%20Extension%20Studio. Pasted a fake ghp_ token and pressed Enter: it was spent against GitHub, refused with 'GitHub rejected that token, so it has not been stored.', and Secret barn-settings stayed empty - which is the promised write path exercised end to end. The design's 'stored per user' half is false and the card says so: 'in this build it is not - there is one Secret for this Rancher's Studio and everybody using it uses the same credential.'

The neutral button reads 'Connect' with no token and 'Reconnect' with one (both observed). Clicking it reveals the token field and focuses it (document.activeElement was settings-github-token). It re-runs the credential exchange rather than an OAuth authorisation - there is no OAuth app in this product - so 'the expiry date moves on afterwards' could not be shown, and no token GitHub accepts exists here.

Enumerated every icon and aria-label in Rancher's header on /barn/settings: menu-icon, the cluster chips, the app group icons, 'Open notification center', 'Open user menu'. There is no grid glyph and no app-collection switcher. Rancher has none for barn to draw.

The header on /barn/settings shows the SUSE chameleon wordmark reading 'SUSE Rancher Prime' (confirmed on a screenshot of the page; the img [data-testid="header__brand-img"] is Rancher's own brand asset and this instance is branded Prime).

On /barn/settings there is no [data-testid="page-actions-menu-action-button"] in the header at all (count 0), where on /barn/editor and /barn/extensions there is one. Studio registers STUDIO_PAGE_ACTIONS through @shell/mixins/page-actions in editor.vue and extensions.vue only; pages/settings.vue does not use the mixin, so the settings route contributes nothing to Rancher's page-actions menu and Rancher draws none of its own.

Clicked the bell ([data-testid="notifications-center"]) on /barn/settings: a .notification-dropdown opened with a 'Notifications' header, 'Mark all as read', and real entries, e.g. 'Code approved - Today, 10:50:29 pm - Committed as d1b3c72, and the code review is recorded against it in Default Admin's name.'

The blue note at the foot of the sign-off card is headed 'Nobody reviews the same extension forty times' and says changes accumulate against the last published version, there is no per-change approval, the run is collapsed into one diff at the push, and '"Notified" means the person who asked gets the criteria checked against the build; it never blocks the push.'

The last card's head reads 'Shown here so you can answer this question without asking the platform team. These rows are what this build does, which is not what the design promises: the design has two of them redacted and Studio redacts nothing.'

The third row uses a warning glyph, not a lock, and reads 'The design promises two things: redaction on the way out, and a scan again before publish. The scan is real, the redaction is not.' The second half of the claim does hold and I proved it: I seeded verify-w5-preflight.yaml in the base pod containing a fake ghp_ token and the publish dialog's credential row turned red with '1 possible credential in the diff ... verify-w5-preflight.yaml:3 looks like a GitHub personal access token.'
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: nothing redacts anything before the request leaves. The pod's ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin and the GitHub token sits in a Secret that pod can read, so a credential the assistant opens goes to the model as written. Making the design's promise true needs something between the assistant and the cluster that does not exist.

verdicts.evidence: The second data row uses a warning glyph rather than a check and says 'The design promises kinds, fields and counts with the values redacted. Studio does not redact: the pod's ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin, so anything the assistant reads from this cluster - values included - can end up in a request.'
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's promise (values stripped) is not implemented and the page says so rather than pretending.

verdicts.evidence: The first data row carries a check glyph (SIcon name=check, class settings__model-icon--sent) and reads 'Your message and the extension source files - Everything under the extension folder in the pod, plus whatever the assistant opens while it works. claude runs in the pod, so the conversation goes to Anthropic's API.'

There is no Save or Apply button anywhere on the page (the page states this itself under the title). Clicked 'Notified' on the developer-load code-review control, navigated away to /barn/editor and back to /barn/settings, and the control still read Notified with nothing pressed in between; the ConfigMap barn-studio-settings had been rewritten on the click. Same for the repository outcome control (Off / Required / Notified each landed in the ConfigMap immediately) and for the custom-role choice.

The 'Push to a repository' row's code-review control shows Required selected with all three segments disabled. Force-clicked 'Off': it stayed Required. The row's reason says why it is fixed rather than merely locked - distributionGate() refuses the distribution until a code sign-off covering the packet is on record - and I saw the gate do exactly that: with no packet, the publish dialog's two gated rows read 'Never handed over' and were not tickable.

Moved the repository outcome control through all three values. Each write landed in ConfigMap barn-studio-settings immediately (read back: off, required, notified) and survived a reload. Each choice also changes what the publish dialog says on that destination: at Required the row reads 'Settings require both sign-offs here, which is what the gate enforces.'; at Off it reads 'Settings put an outcome sign-off at "Off". The gate takes both regardless...'; at Notified 'Settings put an outcome sign-off at "Notified". The gate takes both regardless...'. Restored to Notified.

The radio is rendered with `disabled` and unchecked; the card's banner says the level is not settable and names what decides it. detectPermission() read the pod's claude-session.sh and reported --dangerously-skip-permissions, so 'Do not ask at all' carries the 'In force' chip instead.
verdicts.defect: Still not selectable here, so the promised behaviour cannot be produced from this page. It needs --dangerously-skip-permissions dropped from pod/claude-session.sh and a way for PodTerminal to surface claude's approval prompts. Note that the editor's session strip now does offer a live mode menu (I switched the pod from 'Edits apply without asking' to 'Planning only, no edits' and back), but claude's own cycle has no 'ask before every file edit' mode in it, so even that cannot produce this level.

verdicts.evidence: The radio is disabled and unchecked; 'Do not ask at all' is the one carrying 'In force'. So this is neither selectable nor the default.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged on this page. detectPermission() already recognises --permission-mode acceptEdits, so the card would follow the moment pod/claude-session.sh changed. The editor's session strip can now cycle the running claude to 'File edits apply, everything else asks' (verified live), but that is a per-session cycle in the pod, not this card, and a restarted session comes back on the bundle's flag.

verdicts.evidence: The card's banner opens 'Not settable, and not per user.' and explains that the flag is one line of claude-session.sh in the extension's seed ConfigMap, that Studio rewrites that ConfigMap from the bundle on every page load, and that everybody with a terminal in the pod is at the same level.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's scope claim (per user, applies from the next message) does not hold. It is per pod and it takes effect when a session next starts.

verdicts.evidence: This is the level in force - the row is checked, carries an 'In force' success chip and an 'Admins only, not enforced' warning chip - but it is not a choice (the radio is disabled) and the row itself says the other two halves of the promise are false: 'nothing restricts who may open a terminal, and the pod's ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin'.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: not a choice, 'admins only' is not enforced, and 'still cannot publish' is false because the publish path runs from a cluster-admin pod.

verdicts.evidence: The Preview cluster control renders as a static row reading 'local - K3s v1.36.1' with a lock glyph. There is no select, no chevron and no menu. The hint under it says Studio creates every pod in the local cluster, named once in extensions.ts rather than read from a setting.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: no cluster picker and nothing for one to write to. This Rancher also has only one cluster, so there would be nothing to pick between.

verdicts.evidence: The card head reads 'Unpublished extensions only ever load on this cluster. A preview is served by the extension's own pod in namespace barn, reached through this cluster's API proxy, so nothing outside this Rancher can load it.' Consistent with what the editor's preview frame actually loads: /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/.

The matrix head has two columns, 'CODE REVIEW' (SIcon name=code) and 'OUTCOME SIGN-OFF' (SIcon name=eye), and every one of the four destination rows renders two independent segmented controls under them, with aria-labels of the form '<destination>: code review' and '<destination>: outcome sign-off'. They are genuinely independent: on the repository row the code column is fixed at Required while the outcome column moved freely through all three values.
The card head reads 'Everything before the push to a repository is iteration, and Studio never interrupts it. The gate is the moment the extension becomes installable by somebody else.'
Heading reads 'Studio settings' over 'Applies to everyone who uses Studio on this Rancher.', with a further line saying there is no Save button on the page.
